questions.question: What is a callout, in Salesforce terms?
options: A way to send an HTTP request from Salesforce to an external system and receive a response
A type of validation rule
A scheduled report that emails a user
A Flow screen component
questions.explanation: A callout is Salesforce (via Apex, Flow, or another tool) sending an HTTP request out to an external system — a REST or SOAP API, a payment gateway, an ERP — and getting back a response.

questions.question: In a synchronous callout, does the user wait for the response?
options: Yes — execution is blocking, and the next step only happens after the response arrives
No — the user never waits for a synchronous callout
Only if the callout fails
It depends on the HTTP method used, not on sync vs async
questions.explanation: Synchronous callouts are blocking: Salesforce waits for the response before continuing to the next line of code, and the user waits for that to resolve.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the standard ways to make an asynchronous callout in Apex?
options: @future method
Queueable Apex
Batch Apex (with Database.AllowsCallouts)
A standard validation rule
questions.explanation: Async callouts run through @future methods, Queueable Apex, Batch Apex (implementing Database.AllowsCallouts), or Scheduled Apex — not through declarative validation rules, which can't make callouts at all.

questions.question: Do synchronous and asynchronous callouts share the same governor limits (100 callouts per transaction, 120-second combined timeout)?
options: No, asynchronous callouts have no limits
Yes — both are subject to the same callout limits per transaction
Only synchronous callouts are limited
The limits only apply in sandbox orgs, not production
questions.explanation: The 100-callouts/120-seconds-per-transaction limit applies to both synchronous and asynchronous contexts — async just means the limit applies to a background transaction instead of the user's foreground one.

questions.question: A nightly job needs to sync thousands of records with an external ERP, and nobody is waiting on screen for it to finish. Which approach fits best?
options: A synchronous callout triggered from a button click
An asynchronous callout (e.g. Batch Apex or Scheduled Apex), since it's long-running and no immediate response is needed
A validation rule
A Visualforce page refresh
questions.explanation: Large-volume, long-running work where nothing is waiting for an instant answer is exactly what asynchronous callouts are for — the job runs in the background and the user isn't blocked.
